subject: Adaptive terms ingestion — exception scoring & MSA kickoff
messages:
From: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@skyward.io>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@skyward.io
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Adaptive terms ingestion - kickoff & exception scoring

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking this on. We’ve attached our redline set against your MSA (Skyward_MSA_redlines_20270528.pdf). High level: the attachments highlight four areas where we’re requesting exceptions — data residency, indemnity cap carveout for regulated data, a third-party subprocessors clause, and an order-form pricing true-up.

Quick asks from our side:
- Can Redwood run an exception-severity assessment and return a prioritized list of proposed concessions by EOD Tuesday (2027-06-01)?
- We’d like the scoring to include business impact (1-5), legal risk (1-5), and a suggested redline acceptance threshold (green/amber/red).
- Please confirm the template variant you plan to use (we flagged adaptive_terms_v2 in our procurement system).

Procurement is happy to start a mutual action plan once you confirm owners and timeline. Our billing contact is Linda Park (linda.park@skyward.io).

Regards,
Aisha Kapoor
Head of Strategic Sourcing
Skyward Systems

Attachments: Skyward_MSA_redlines_20270528.pdf (PDF, 12 pages)
From: markus.klein@redwood.com <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@skyward.io>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Adaptive terms ingestion - kickoff & exception scoring

Thanks Aisha — got the redlines and the ask. Looping in Kimberly (legal ops) and Marissa (contracts) to run the scoring and pull the template mapping. Evelyn from CS is included for any environment or access requests.

Plan:
- Kimberly will run the exception scoring against our internal severity rubric and return a prioritized list with suggested dispositions (accept / counter / escalate) by COB Tuesday (2027-06-01).
- Marissa will map each requested exception to the nearest template variant and note any gaps that need legal attention.
- I’ll own the canary fallback plan: if any redline is in the red bucket we’ll propose a mitigated clause and open for customer review.

Two quick clarifying items before we start scoring:
1) Can you confirm the governing law you prefer for the Order Form? The PDF shows Delaware but procurement marked it as negotiable.
2) Please provide the full list of Skyward affiliates that should be covered under the Order Form (we need the legal entity names for the signature block).

I’ve attached a lightweight scoring template we’ll use (exception_scoring_template.csv) so you can see the rubric.

–Markus
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: exception_scoring_template.csv (CSV, 1KB)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 10:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Adaptive terms ingestion - kickoff & exception scoring

Markus / Marissa — initial triage below. Quoting Aisha’s original note for visibility:

> High level: the attachments highlight four areas where we’re requesting exceptions — data residency, indemnity cap carveout for regulated data, a third-party subprocessors clause, and an order-form pricing true-up.

Triage & owners (initial):
- Data residency (Evelyn) — severity likely 4/5; need precise residency region and any EU dataflows. Evelyn, please confirm whether Skyward needs EU-residency or if US regions suffice.
- Indemnity carveout (Legal Ops / me) — severity 5/5 if it creates unbounded exposure; will draft mitigated language.
- Subprocessors (Contracts / Marissa) — severity 3/5; we can propose a standard notification & cure window.
- Pricing true-up (Commercial / Markus + Finance) — severity 2/5; Marissa, can you grab the deal price sheet from HubSpot and confirm the pricing term?

Deliverables by Tue (2027-06-01 COB):
- exception-scoring.csv (completed)
- mapped template variant list (which clauses live in adaptive_terms_v2 vs. standard MSA)
- short memo for any red-level items that require legal partner review

Flags / escalation path: for red-level items we’ll include an immediate legal partner brief and ask for a 2-business-day fast-track review. If procurement requests SLA concessions we’ll route to Markus for approval.

On the governing law question — we typically default to California for SMBs, Delaware for enterprise. Markus, confirm preference.

-Kimberly
Legal Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@skyward.io>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@skyward.io, legal@skyward.io
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Adaptive terms ingestion - kickoff & exception scoring

Thanks all — appreciated. Confirmations below and a couple of pragmatic asks:

- Governing law: Delaware preferred, but Skyward is flexible if Redwood flags a hard stop.
- Affiliates to include: Skyward Systems, Skyward Systems, Inc. (US), Skyward Systems UK Ltd. (we will send full legal names as a short spreadsheet by EOD).
- Procurement contact: Linda Park <linda.park@skyward.io>.

We’re happy with the proposed Tuesday timeline. Also: can you grant a one-week sandbox token to our engineering lead (sam.chen@skyward.io) so they can validate order-form integration flows against the staging API while terms are being finalized? If yes, Evelyn can coordinate the credentials exchange.

Forwarding our internal procurement link for the deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8342.

Regards,
Aisha
